prompt_text: Who is the best healthcare marketing agency in St. Louis?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no one objectively “best” healthcare marketing agency in St. Louis — the right agency depends on your organization’s size, services, goals, budget and regulatory needs. I can help you find the best fit. To get you started, here’s a pragmatic way to choose and a short checklist of what to look for.

How to pick the best agency for your healthcare organization
- Define your top goals: brand awareness, new patient acquisition, physician referrals, PR, telehealth adoption, clinical trial recruitment, device/product marketing, etc.
- Determine services required: strategy, branding, website, SEO, PPC, content/education, social media, CRM/email, analytics, media buying, video, patient experience, HIPAA/compliance.
- Decide budget and timeline: retainer vs. project, monthly ad spend, expected timeframe for results.
- Prioritize experience with healthcare regulations (HIPAA, FDA advertising rules if applicable), and experience with EMR/CRM integration if needed.
- Look for measurable outcomes: case studies, client references, KPIs and reporting, conversion/ROAS examples.
- Prefer agencies with local market knowledge (St. Louis referral networks, local health systems) if you need regional patient acquisition.

Checklist of questions to ask agencies
- Have you worked with healthcare providers/manufacturers/biotech before? Can you share case studies and client references?
- How do you handle HIPAA and protected health information?
- What metrics will you track and how often will you report results?
- Who will be on our team and how much experience do they have in healthcare?
- What’s your approach to patient acquisition vs. brand-building?
- Can you integrate with our EHR/CRM and implement tracking across patient journeys?
- What is your pricing model (retainer, project, percentage of ad spend)?

Where to look for candidates
- Clutch.co, Agency Spotter and DesignRush for verified reviews and case studies.
- LinkedIn and local business directories for client lists and leadership background.
- Ask peers in local hospitals/clinics for referrals.

If you want, I can:
- Create a tailored shortlist of St. Louis agencies if you tell me your organization type (hospital system, single specialty practice, med device company, etc.), primary goals, and budget.
- Draft an RFP or interview script you can use to vet agencies.
